headline_marked: ThonburianTTS: [[Free Thai AI TTS runs locally, clones voices]] by Thai researchers
headline: ThonburianTTS: Free Thai AI TTS runs locally, clones voices by Thai researchers
summary: Developed by Mahidol University and Looloo Technology, ThonburianTTS offers natural Thai text-to-speech with zero-shot voice cloning, available for free on HuggingFace and GitHub.
details: ThonburianTTS is a new Thai Text-to-Speech (TTS) model that runs locally, offers natural-sounding speech, and supports voice cloning. Developed by a research team from Mahidol University and Looloo Technology, it was presented at iSAI-NLP 2025.

This model is freely available on HuggingFace and GitHub, making it an accessible option for developers and users seeking a Thai TTS solution without API costs. It's built upon the F5-TTS (Flow Matching) architecture, utilizing diffusion-based flow matching for natural speech generation.

ThonburianTTS excels in generating accurate and natural Thai pronunciation, outperforming many multilingual models not specifically optimized for the language. Users can clone voices with short audio samples, typically 5-10 seconds, with reported similarity scores between 84-89%.

The model can run on both GPU (NVIDIA CUDA) for faster processing and CPU, though CPU performance will be slower. A Gradio Web UI is also provided on HuggingFace Spaces for immediate testing without any installation.

However, ThonburianTTS has limitations: it is not ideal for generating long texts, as it was trained on the GigaSpeech2 dataset which focuses on shorter utterances. Newer models like JaiTTS may offer better zero-shot speaker cloning capabilities.

Inference typically requires about 2-3 GB of VRAM for GPU usage. Additionally, the current license restricts commercial use. For projects requiring long-form text generation or commercial applications, alternatives like JaiTTS or Qwen-TTS might be more suitable.

headline_marked: [[Andrew Ng open-sources OpenWorker]], an AI coworker desktop app that gets tasks done
headline: Andrew Ng open-sources OpenWorker, an AI coworker desktop app that gets tasks done
summary: OpenWorker is a desktop app that uses AI to complete tasks across files, terminals, and other applications, delivering actual finished work instead of just chat responses. It runs locally with your own API keys for privacy.
details: Andrew Ng has open-sourced OpenWorker, a desktop application designed as an "AI coworker" that delivers completed tasks rather than just chat responses. Within three weeks, the project garnered over 13,700 stars and 1,900 forks on GitHub, indicating strong interest in AI that "gets work done."

Unlike conversational AIs such as ChatGPT or Claude, OpenWorker operates as a desktop app, allowing AI to work across your files, terminal, and other applications. It focuses on creating actual deliverables, not just offering advice or to-do lists.

A key feature is its privacy-preserving design: everything runs locally on your machine using your own API keys. Data only leaves your device through the specific models and integrations you choose, ensuring user control over information.

OpenWorker is built on `aisuite`, a unified LLM provider library developed by Andrew Ng, which enables seamless switching between different LLM providers without code changes. It boasts over 25 native connectors, including a bidirectional Slack integration where mentioning @OpenWorker in a channel triggers tasks on your desktop, with replies sent back to the thread.

The project exemplifies "Loop Engineering," a concept where AI agents are set up to continuously prompt other AIs to complete complex tasks autonomously. OpenWorker's design allows it to pause and seek approval before executing actions that could have significant impact, such as sending messages or changing calendar entries.

While fully usable and actively being polished, OpenWorker is currently best suited for individual users and small teams. The team notes there are still rough edges, with over 170 open issues and 228 pull requests on GitHub, and some workflows are not yet fully complete.

It operates as a local desktop app with no cloud version, centralized administration, or SSO/SCIM, making it less suitable for large organizations requiring enterprise governance. There is no vendor SLA, enterprise support contract, or third-party security certifications yet.
